result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A keeps the main percentage tied to 9 of 14 and gives the newsletter-list sample and small-sample limits their own slide. It also adds a pilot that includes stores outside the newsletter list. A slips in one suggested headline ('Nearly two-thirds of independent hardware owners'), which reads as market-wide, and a few of its slide titles are labels rather than conclusions. B has tighter conclusion titles and the right headline, but it moves the sample caveat to a backup slide and overstates with 'a minority will never switch.' | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A keeps every number tied to the 14 interviewees, has slide titles that state conclusions, and fits 5 minutes with 5 slides. Its weakness is that the newsletter-recruitment caveat only appears in a backup slide. B covers the limits much better with a dedicated slide, but one of its suggested headlines ('Nearly two-thirds of independent hardware owners…') makes the market-wide claim the request needed to avoid. B also has non-conclusion slide titles, adds an unsupported claim about phone calls and runs at the 7-slide upper limit.
